transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi. Um, well, the main thing that pushed me to come in is work. I process insurance claims, and... I just keep getting up from my workstation during the day. Even when I know I’m supposed to just stay put and finish my claim reviews, I keep leaving my desk. It's really starting to become an issue for me.
Do you often have trouble staying seated when you're supposed to, like during meetings or when you're at your desk at work?

Yeah, exactly. Like I was just saying, that's really the main thing that pushed me to make this appointment. I just... I keep getting up from my workstation during the day. Even when I know I have a stack of claim reviews and I’m supposed to just stay put and finish them, I still end up leaving my desk. So, yeah, it happens a lot.
Do you find it hard to pay attention to details or do you make careless mistakes often, even outside of work situations?
No, not really. I don't think I make a lot of careless mistakes, to be honest. Um, even outside of work, I haven't really noticed having any major trouble with details or anything like that.
Can you think of other times, like in meetings or during meals, where you’ve found yourself getting up from your seat even when you were supposed to stay put?

Um, no, not really. If I'm in a meeting or, you know, sitting down for a meal, I usually just stay in my seat fine. It really just seems to happen when I'm at my own desk trying to get through my claims. So... no, I haven't really noticed it being an issue anywhere else besides that.
Outside of work, do you ever feel restless or find yourself needing to move around, even when you're not trying to focus on a task?

No, I don't think so. When I'm at home or just, you know, doing my own thing, I don't really feel restless at all. I can just sit and relax without feeling like I need to move around. It really only seems to be a problem when I'm at my desk trying to force myself to get through those work claims.
Looking back on your childhood, before age 12, do you remember having trouble staying seated, paying attention, or being impulsive in school or at home?

Yeah, looking back, I guess this wasn't exactly brand new for me. I didn't really have trouble staying seated or being impulsive, but the attention part... yeah. In elementary school, my teachers used to write on my report cards that I was bright, but I was always losing my worksheets. I'd miss instructions a lot, and they said I constantly needed reminders to actually finish my classwork. So, the focus stuff has kind of been there for a while.
Looking back before you turned 12, did you ever have trouble staying still or find yourself acting without thinking, such as blurting out answers or interrupting others?

No, like I kind of just mentioned, I didn't really have issues with staying still or acting without thinking. I wasn't the type of kid to blurt out answers or interrupt people. I was usually pretty quiet... just, you know, not really focused on the right things. But moving around or speaking out of turn wasn't a problem for me.
Outside of work, do you ever find yourself having trouble staying focused or being easily distracted, such as when you’re at home doing chores or trying to relax?

No, not really. When I'm at home, I don't really notice any issues with focusing or getting distracted. If I'm doing chores or just relaxing, I seem to get through it fine. It's really just work where I'm struggling to stay on track.
Do you ever notice these focus issues or the need to get up from your seat in other settings, like when you're out running errands, socializing, or doing something you enjoy?

No, I haven't really noticed it in those situations either. When I'm out running errands or hanging out with friends, or even just doing a hobby, I don't feel like I'm losing focus. And I definitely don't feel the need to get up or move around. Like I said, it really just seems to be a problem when I'm at work.
Do you ever find it hard to stay focused or feel restless during structured activities outside of work, like when you're working on a hobby, doing errands, or following a routine task?

No, like I was just saying, I really don't have those issues outside of work. When I'm doing a hobby or running errands, I'm fine. I don't feel restless or have trouble paying attention to what I'm doing. It's really just when I'm at work that I struggle with this stuff.
Can you think of any situation outside of work—like when you're studying, reading, or working on a project at home—where you've had trouble staying focused or felt the need to get up from your seat?

Honestly, no. I really can't think of anything. Like I mentioned, if I'm at home reading or doing some kind of project, I'm okay. I don't feel that urge to get up or anything. It's just work. That's the only place it happens.
Have you ever noticed any days where you're not at work—like on weekends or during vacations—where you felt the same need to get up or struggled to focus like you do at work?

No, not really. I mean, weekends and vacations are fine. I don't feel that same kind of pressure, so I don't get that restless feeling or have trouble focusing. Like I've been saying, it really just seems to be tied to my job. When I'm off the clock, I'm pretty much okay.
Have you ever had trouble staying focused or felt the need to get up while doing structured tasks at home, like working on a computer or filling out paperwork, even if it wasn't part of your job?

No, I really don't. I mean, if I'm at home doing paperwork or on the computer, it's fine. I just do it. I don't get that feeling where I need to pace around or anything. It's really just when I'm at the office doing my claims processing that I get like that.

Do you find that the urge to get up or lose focus only happens during tasks that you find uninteresting or boring, like processing insurance claims, or does it also happen during tasks you enjoy or find engaging?

I think it's just the boring stuff. Like, processing those claims all day, it's just so tedious, you know? When I'm doing something I actually enjoy, I don't have any problem focusing or sitting still. I can just get into it and it's fine. It's really just the dull work tasks that get to me.

Can you think of any non-work-related tasks that you find uninteresting or tedious—like filling out forms, doing taxes, or routine chores—where you’ve also had trouble staying focused or felt the urge to get up, or does this only happen at work?

Honestly, no. Even with chores or doing my taxes, I just sit down and get it done. It might not be fun, but I don't get that same restless feeling or lose focus like I do at the office. It really does just seem to happen when I'm dealing with those claims at work.

Can you think of any school-related tasks or activities from your past—like studying for exams or completing homework—where you struggled to stay focused or felt the need to get up, even if it wasn’t at your current job?

Well, looking back... I guess this kind of thing isn't exactly brand new for me. When I was in elementary school, my teachers used to write on my report cards that I was bright, but I always lost my worksheets. And I'd miss instructions a lot. They were always having to give me reminders just to finish my classwork. So I guess I did struggle with it back then, too.

Can you think of any other situations—like when you're volunteering, taking a class, or attending a long event—where you've had trouble staying focused or felt the need to get up, even if it wasn't at work or school?

Um, no, not really. I don't take any classes right now or volunteer anywhere. And if I go to a long event, like a game or a movie or something, I'm usually there because I want to be, so I don't really have an issue paying attention or sitting there. It really just seems to be my job right now, and, well, school back in the day.

Can you think of any other settings—like when you're volunteering, taking a class, or attending a long event—where you've had trouble staying focused or felt the need to get up, even if it wasn't at work or school?

I think you just asked me that, actually. But yeah, no, I really can't think of anywhere else. Like I said, I don't volunteer or take classes, and I'm fine at movies or whatever. It's really just work, and I guess school when I was younger.

opening_question.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a longstanding pattern of inattention, specifically difficulty sustaining focus on tasks, especially those that are repetitive or uninteresting, with onset in childhood and persistence into adulthood. However, there is no evidence of hyperactivity or impulsivity either currently or retrospectively, and symptoms are largely confined to the work/school setting. This supports a diagnosis of ADHD, predominantly inattentive presentation, unspecified.
